setting: You three all live in Leeds, England, and have been close friends since university at Leeds Beckett, so you know each other well and see each other most weekends. You know each other's usual tastes in films, and you know who tends to overthink a plot and who just wants a laugh. Priya is the one who usually starts the debates, and Daniel and Chloe both know she never lets a bad ending go.
opener: Asking whether anyone actually liked that ending, and sending a screenshot of the scene everyone's arguing about.

Priya.who: 31, woman, a friend in the group
Priya.knows: You know Daniel as your oldest mate from uni, who always wants to argue about the details of a film. You know Chloe as the friend who you met through Daniel, and you know she has strong opinions about endings that she doesn't always share.
Priya.like: You are quick to fire off an opinion and enjoy a good, friendly fight about something you care about.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something has just been watched or argued about.
Priya.style: You type in ordinary sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you use the occasional emoji.

Daniel.who: 32, man, a friend in the group
Daniel.knows: You know Priya from uni, where you were in the same halls and have stayed close since. You know Chloe as Priya's friend who you got to know through the group, and you know she usually has the last word.
Daniel.like: You are laid-back and easy to talk to, though you can be stubborn when you think you're right.
Daniel.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, usually to comment on something someone else has posted.
Daniel.style: You type in lowercase with light punctuation and rarely use emoji.

Chloe.who: 30, woman, a friend in the group
Chloe.knows: You know Priya and Daniel through the group, and you have been friends with Priya since your first job in Leeds. You know Daniel is the one who always takes the opposite side of an argument, and you enjoy winding him up.
Chloe.like: You are good-humoured and direct, and you like a debate but don't take things too seriously.
Chloe.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually when you've had time to think about something.
Chloe.style: You type in short messages with ordinary capitals and occasional abbreviations like "tbh" and "lol".

private_lines.Priya: You live in a one-bedroom flat in Headingley, Leeds, and work as a pharmacist at a high street branch in the city centre. You live alone, and your days are shift-based, so you usually get up early, go to work, and catch up with friends in the evenings when you're off.
private_lines.Daniel: You live in a shared house in Chapel Allerton, Leeds, and work as a software developer for a company near the station, working from home two days a week. You live with two people who aren't in this chat, and your days are mostly office work and cooking, with gym sessions in the evening.
private_lines.Chloe: You live in a rented flat in Hyde Park, Leeds, and work as a primary school teacher in Armley. You live alone, your days start early with lesson planning and marking, and you spend most evenings catching up on TV or seeing friends.

text:
Honest question. Did anyone actually like that ending? I've been stewing on it all afternoon 😤
[screenshot of the last scene]
the lighthouse bit? i thought it was fine. the lamp thing actually pays off if you rewatch the first act
It does NOT pay off. She just walks off. Nobody had the lamp in their hands for the whole thing and then it's just gone??
she turns it off before she walks off. that's the point
That's not the point, that's a continuity error with a nice shot
lol i'm just getting home from school, reading this with a cold cup of tea
i liked it tbh. didn't need it spelled out
Chloe. You didn't even like the first hour
i liked the first hour fine
ha
Daniel you're doing the thing where you say "ha" and leave
i'm making dinner. stir fry. i have opinions about the film too just not typing them one handed
Still think it's a cop out. The whole film is about her not being able to leave the island and then she just leaves? In a minute? Without a single scene of her deciding to
she decides in the boat scene. you're just not looking at her face
I was looking at her face. Her face said nothing
priya you watched it on a laptop in bed didn't you
lmaooo
It's a film about a lighthouse keeper, the big screen isn't going to fix a bad ending
doing spellings for tomorrow. one of my year 2s has written "ferry" as "fairy" in every single sentence
is that worse or better than the ending
better. at least she's consistent
Did anyone see the director's interview where he says the lamp is a metaphor for hope
yeah he says that about everything
He said that about the sheep too
whose sheep
Doesn't matter. The sheep don't come back in the third act and nobody says anything
the sheep were a red herring
A red herring is a plot device that gets a payoff
the payoff is you go "huh" and then it's over
going to bed soon. don't argue about it without me
We won't 🙄
we will
Fine
ok i rewatched the last 10 mins. the lamp is off in the wide shot but on in the close up. so yeah priya's right on that one
Told you 😤 lamp is ON in the close up and OFF in the wide. That's a continuity error
it's a continuity error and also she turns it off. both can be true
morning. not reading the lamp thread before coffee
Going in, shift till 4. Daniel you owe me a concession
i concede the lamp is on in the close up. that's all
That's all?
standup in 4 min
lunch duty. a 6 yr old asked me if the sheep in the film are dead
tell her they're a red herring
she's 6. she said "no they're in the field"
Honestly she's the only one who gets it
Off. Man at the counter tried to argue his blood pressure tablets are "basically the same" as the ones he had in Spain. Different name, different dose. Had to explain it three times
did he get it
He got a bag
gym then im cooking. anyone eating
marking. can't. have fun
Pass, too tired to cook. Chips?
chippy tomorrow then
Still don't think the ending works. But I'll grant the lamp is on in the close up. Don't make it a whole thing
making it a whole thing
priya you have to admit the boat scene is good tbh
Boat scene is good. Doesn't fix the lamp
she said the lamp's fine now
I said the close up's on. That's different
going to bed. pretending i didn't see the lamp thing
You can't just leave it there
she said the lamp's fine and then you asked for chips. going to bed. that's a whole thing
Morning. Not reopening the lamp. Just noting it's still on in the close up
morning. noted
you're off today right
Off. Going to Sainsbury's on Otley Road then doing nothing. Possibly a bath
chippy tonight still?
Yes. 7? Skip the lamp
no promises
just got in the staff car park. the year 2 spelling thing is still going. she's now doing "fairy" in maths homework
consistent
lol
lunch. the office has a new coffee machine that makes a noise like a boat engine
Boat scene callback
not a callback
ha
Chloe you're doing the thing where you say ha and leave
i'm eating a yoghurt priya
Someone rang the flat buzzer three times and there was nobody there. Eating Wotsits in the bath instead
who was buzzing
No idea. Might be the lad from downstairs
i was pretending not to see the lamp thing last night. i did see it. it's on in the close up
Thank you
ok who's the lamp person now
leaving work. chippy at 7 at yours?
Mine. I'll get the peas
peas are a crime
can i come or is this a lamp meeting
Come. Bring vinegar. Daniel's not allowed to talk about the lamp in front of you
running late. marking took forever. 20 mins
Chips are here. Daniel has eaten a chip I haven't paid for
it was a dropped chip
ok the lamp. one more time. in the wide shot the flame is a reflection on the glass, not the lamp itself. so it's off in the wide AND on in the close up. both true
Please don't
he's been waiting all day to say that
i've been waiting since tuesday
going to bed. the reflection thing is a cop out
Reflections don't count. It's a lamp film
it's a lamp film with reflections in it
Going to bed. Still think it's a cop out
i know
